cds.title: Michigan Technological University Common Data Set 2025-2026 (xlsx)

scorecard.title: College Scorecard (location, enrollment, cost; data released 2026-10-15)

stats.notes: From the Common Data Set (Fall 2025 entering class, C1): 10,359 applied, 8,853 admitted (85.5%), 1,448 enrolled; residency rows (in-state 6,047 / out-of-state 3,428 / international 884 applicants) add up to the totals. International first-years: 884 applied, 845 admitted (95.6%), 9 enrolled. No early decision, no early action and no waitlist (C2, C21, C22). Rolling admission. GPA breakdown covers all enrolled students who reported a GPA (93.5%); the 4.0 row is '4.0+'. Test scores: the CDS lists SAT composite, section and ACT percentiles for the enrolled class; 66% (959 students) submitted SAT and 18% (261) submitted ACT. Undergraduate enrollment (6,009) and the nonresident count (53) are the 'Total Undergraduates' figures in B1/B2.

cost.notes: First-year, full-time costs for the 2026-2027 academic year from the Common Data Set (G1, final figures; the 'not available' box is not ticked): Michigan-resident tuition $20,396, nonresident tuition $46,294 (12-18 credits per semester at the same rate), required fees $382, food and housing on campus $14,321 (housing $8,028 + meal plan $6,293). Estimated expenses (G5): books $1,200, transportation $1,474, other $1,372 (other costs shown = transportation + other). Per-credit rate below 12 credits: $769 resident, $1,714 nonresident. Students with 60+ credits (including AP/IB/dual-enrollment credit) pay upper-division tuition. The university's own tuition page (opened 2026-11-03) lists the same tuition and fees but food and housing of $15,321 (rates vary by residence hall; the CDS figure is $1,000 lower) and an annual total of $66,043 for non-Michigan residents ($40,145 for Michigan residents); that page also says international students pay an extra $250 per semester surcharge (not counted above, no total is entered because the two sources differ). First-year students must live on campus.
